new_statements.translation: Phonetically, Awu has 33 consonants, all simple; 11 vowels, mainly monophthongs; as for tones, there are chiefly three basic tones, 55, 33 and 31; sound changes are chiefly of two types, rhyme change and tone change (sandhi). [TOC:] 2. Tone sandhi. Awu tone sandhi has the following three common cases: (1) high level + high level -> low falling + high level; (2) mid level + low falling -> mid level + high level; (3) mid level + mid level -> mid level + high level.

new_statements.relation_note: Three basic tones 55/33/31; tone sandhi (3 rules); 33 simple consonants; 11 vowels; syllable types section exists (content not visible). No stress/accent statement visible; full text might contain more under （三）声调 and （五）音节类型.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Awu of Yuanyang is a tone language with three basic lexical tones -- high level 55, mid level 33, low falling 31 -- plus disyllabic tone sandhi (55+55 -> 31+55; 33+31 -> 33+55; 33+33 -> 33+55). Nothing is said about word stress or accent in the accessible abstract/TOC.
new_statements.exceptions: Tone values change in context for some items (e.g. directional verbs la31 'come', ʑi31/li33 'go' 'change tone in specific contexts' per TOC 三（五）1(2)); rhyme alternations tɤ33/tv33, tɤ33/to33 noted.
new_statements.identity_note: Explicitly the Awu 阿邬 of Yuanyang County, a Hani-nationality subgroup whose speech the authors class as Yi-branch (Loloish) -- exactly Glottolog's sout2719 (Lu & Lu 2011's Daping/Xiaopingzi Awu; Hsiu 2017's Lawoish Awu). The reported system (33 consonants, three tones 55/33/31) matches Hsiu's second-hand summary of Lu & Lu (55, 33, low-falling). Fieldwork evidently from the July 2023 Yunnan Minzu University survey in Fengchunling township 逢春岭乡 (adjacent to Daping) -- same languoid, possibly a different village. Not the Southeastern-Ngwi Awu [yiu] awuu1235 of Mile/Luxi, and not Northern Awu.
